tldr: Concentrating cluster-period precision in the terminal all-treated period creates a sharp loss in the ability of one precommitted stepped-wedge randomization to protect every unknown plateau horizon and pairwise duration contrast. The proved maximin expected-realized information ratio satisfies the explicit bounds \(\frac{\alpha}{9}\min\{1,M^{-1}+\min\{n,L\}/L^2\}\le c^\star\le\frac92\min\{1,M^{-1}+\min\{n,L\}/L^2\}\). The cluster-abundance elbow is at \(n\asymp L\), the sampling elbow is \(M\asymp L^2/\min\{n,L\}\), and the exact terminal limit remains \(g(n,L)\), including \(2/L\) when \(2L\mid n\) and \(1/\binom L2\) when \(n=2\).
gap: Exposure-time analyses are now well motivated, but available design theory conditions on a specified lag horizon or target, optimizes an immediate effect, or performs maximin optimization over nuisance correlation. It does not explain whether one legal randomization can be uniformly competitive for an unknown plateau horizon and all duration contrasts when sampling becomes concentrated in the terminal period.
